subject: physics
title: Star colour, brightness and the HR diagram
key_idea: A star's colour shows its surface temperature: red stars are cool and blue-white stars are hot. Absolute magnitude measures a star's brightness at a standard distance. The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram plots absolute magnitude against colour and shows the main groups of stars.

blocks.text: Stars are different colours. This section covers what a star's colour tells us.

items: Astronomers classify stars according to their **colour**.
A star's colour is related to its **surface temperature**.
The Sun is yellow, with a surface temperature of about 5600 K.
A red or orange star is cooler than the Sun. A blue-white star is hotter.

blocks.text: (Physics only) Some stars only look bright because they are close. This section covers a fair way to compare them.

items.meaning: How bright a star looks from the Earth. It depends on distance as well as on the star.
A measure of the brightness of a star at a standard distance.

items: The standard distance is 10 parsecs, which is about 32.6 light-years.
Using one distance for every star makes the comparison fair.
Absolute magnitude is a measure of the star's real brightness, also called luminosity or power.
A smaller (or more negative) number means a brighter star.
Star D has the lowest number, so it is by far the brightest star in the table.
Two stars can look equally bright from the Earth if the more powerful one is further away.
Absolute magnitude is brightness at a standard distance.
Using a standard distance removes the effect of how far away the star is.

blocks.text: (Physics only) The HR diagram plots every star as one point. This section covers its axes and its main groups.

items: The vertical axis is **absolute magnitude** (brightness). Brighter stars are at the top.
The horizontal axis is **colour**, which shows surface temperature. Hot, blue-white stars are on the left and cool, red stars are on the right.
The diagram shows how absolute magnitude relates to colour.
Supergiants are at the very top. Red giants are just below them on the right.
Only stars appear on it. The Moon does not, because it does not emit its own light.
To draw it, label both axes, then sketch the main sequence band, the giants at the top right and the white dwarfs at the bottom left.

Most stars lie on the main sequence, a diagonal band.

checks.q: State what is meant by absolute magnitude.
checks.a: A measure of the brightness of a star at a standard distance.

checks.q: Rigel is blue and Betelgeuse is red. State which has the higher surface temperature and why.
checks.a: Rigel, because a star's colour depends on its surface temperature and blue stars are hotter than red stars.

checks.q: Suggest why a powerful star and a weak star can appear equally bright from the Earth.
checks.a: The weaker star is closer to the Earth than the more powerful star.

worked_example.question: The table gives information about four different stars in the same galaxy as the Sun. Antares is red, Capella is yellow, Sirius B is white and Vega is blue-white. Explain how the stars can be classified according to their colour.
answer_points: The colour of a star depends on its temperature.
In order from coolest to hottest: Antares (red), Capella (yellow), Sirius B (white), Vega (blue-white).
worked_example.tip: Link colour to temperature, then give the full order.
